strata.text: The Strait of Hormuz closes — the chokepoint the Carter Doctrine was written to keep open
The United States goes to war with Iran
180 million barrels released after Russia invades Ukraine — the largest drawdown in the reserve's history
30.6 million barrels released during the intervention in Libya
11 million barrels released after Hurricane Katrina
17.3 million barrels released during Operation Desert Storm
U.S. Central Command established, giving the doctrine a standing army
The Carter Doctrine declares the Persian Gulf a vital U.S. interest, to be defended by force
Congress creates the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
The oil embargo. Everything above this layer follows from it.

quote.text: An attempt by any outside force to gain control of the Persian Gulf region will be regarded as an assault on the vital interests of the United States of America, and such an assault will be repelled by any means necessary, including military force.
quote.attribution: Jimmy Carter, State of the Union address, January 23, 1980

sources.label: Carter Doctrine, State of the Union 1980
